# Dependency import fixture provenance

These fixtures exercise specific exported formats, not every vendor API or CSV report. Vendor findings and reachability claims are input to validation, not validation results.

- `snyk.json` is a synthetic fixture with the field structure of the JSON example in [Snyk's reachability documentation](https://github.com/snyk/user-docs/blob/7c00c25e09a04acb9505886928ad04f6399ef3f8/scan-fix-and-prevent/manage-risk/prioritize-issues-for-fixing/reachability-analysis.md), with invented package names, paths, advisory IDs, and descriptions. The accepted format is `snyk test --json` / `--json-file-output`, either a single report or the array produced for multiple projects. Another vendor-maintained fixture is [Snyk CLI basic npm results](https://github.com/snyk/cli/blob/efd1c6c82caef6ec1fdccc44d8e3b49009e6453b/test/fixtures/basic-npm/results.json). API `issues.vulnerabilities` and Code/IaC SARIF are separate formats and are not accepted.
- `socket.json` is a synthetic fixture with the field structure of [Socket CLI's captured Python shallow package response](https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-cli/blob/1d82744512967f0588c6c4fc20008c2c933c2f26/src/command/package/fixtures/python_shallow.json). It includes invented malware, license, and quality alerts with synthetic package names, source IDs, paths, and descriptions. The accepted wrapper is `{ "ok": true, "data": [artifacts] }`, or an array of full-scan artifacts. The [Socket SDK OpenAPI](https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-sdk-js/blob/d7073fca8874995b17ac24f3b17021a2e8ba0525/openapi.json) defines `SocketArtifact`, `SocketAlert`, and `ReachabilityResult`. Full-scan HTTP responses use NDJSON: the file reader must decode each line into that artifact array. Package-deep summary objects, CSV, old `issues` reports, and bare alert arrays are not accepted. Alert `start`/`end` positions are not assumed to be line numbers. Graph IDs and source locations remain vendor evidence; they are not fabricated into dependency chains.
- `endor.json` is a **synthetic schema-derived fixture**, not a captured customer or vendor scan. The exact fields and enum values come from [Endor's generated Finding model](https://github.com/endorlabs/endorlabs-sdk/blob/8a41756890c2dee3bb089fee881cae4f2adbde03/src/endorlabs/generated/models/finding_service.py). Endor [documents `.list.objects[]` for list results and a direct object for `api get`](https://docs.endorlabs.com/developers-api/rest-api/using-the-rest-api/masks/). `reachable_paths` contains function paths, not dependency chains. Support is limited to unmasked Finding objects / ListFindingsResponse JSON with the necessary finding metadata; Query response wrappers and aggregate counts are not accepted. No claim of end-to-end compatibility with a live Endor export is made by this fixture.

- `endor.csv` is **synthetic**, using the Endor findings export column names and cell encodings. All fixture values, identities, descriptions, advisories, and paths are invented; no tenant records are included. It covers quoted commas, quotes and multiline cells, dependency ecosystem URIs, scoped npm packages, vulnerability and malware categories, and missing metadata. The default export is recognized by `UUID`, `Title`, `Severity Level`, and `Finding Categories`; absent package or location columns leave findings visible with warnings. Include `Dependency Name`, `Location`, `Aliases`, `Remediation`, `Fix Version`, and `Commit SHA` when exporting to retain those details. `Package Name` describes source package context and is not substituted for `Dependency Name`. Comma-containing location cells remain vendor evidence because individual paths cannot be distinguished from filenames containing commas. Absolute locations retain their vendor scope. CSV `original` stores the exact parsed row cell values; the importer separately retains the original report text.

Fixtures retain only the field shapes needed to check parsing. All finding identities, package names, descriptions, and paths are synthetic; none are captured scan results. Additional malformed, missing-field, repeated-path, and mixed-category cases are constructed in tests and are not represented as captured exports.

Regression cases also cover Snyk's `--group-issues` array of dependency chains and Socket NDJSON containing only one artifact. These are synthetic transport and grouping cases, not captured vendor exports. Socket `scan report` policy summaries are intentionally rejected; use `scan view` JSON or the full-scan artifact stream.

The parser accepts at most 10,000 source findings, including excluded alerts, before normalization. This bounds local parsing and storage work; it is not a scanner capacity limit. Shared project/package context is limited to 16 KiB and normalized findings to 16 MiB. The importer retains its 8 MiB input limit and 100-finding assessment selection limit. Per-finding Socket evidence keeps package identity, manifest/graph references, and the matching reachability summary; unrelated artifact metadata remains in the original report stored by the importer rather than being duplicated for every alert.
